newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Murdoch rules out bid for Fairfax.
newsitem.headline: Murdoch rules out bid for Fairfax.

text.p: News Corp Ltd chairman and chief executive Rupert Murdoch has ruled out a bid for rival Australian media group John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, the Courier-Mail newspaper reported on Friday.
"I don't want to buy Fairfax. I don't believe Mr (Kerry) Packer wants to buy Fairfax," the newspaper, owned by News Corp subsidiary News Ltd, quoted Murdoch as saying in an interview.

"To my knowledge he (Packer) has three times tried to sell his shares within the last 12 months," Murdoch said. "He'd like to influence and have the power of Fairfax but he's too shrewd to be paying for Fairfax at today's price," Murdoch said.

Murdoch's interests hold a five percent stake in Fairfax, which is about 25 percent owned by Conrad Black's Hollinger International Inc. Packer interests hold about 15 percent of Fairfax, which owns the Sydney Morning Herald, Melbourne's The Age and the Australian Financial Review as well as dailies in Newcastle and Wollongong, New South Wales.

"Daily there are questions about the value of print media against electronic media. I don't think Kerry will be looking to buy Fairfax and I know he wasn't looking to buy it as recently as a few weeks ago," Murdoch said.

Packer also controls television broadcaster Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL), which holds the Fairfax stake. PBL has said it wants to merge with Fairfax but it is prevented from doing so currently by cross-media ownership rules.
Black has also said he wants to boost his stake in Fairfax but he is currently prevented from doing so under government regulations limiting foreign control of Australian media.
The Australian government has said it will review its media ownership regulations.
"I think Mr Black's going to be left with 25 percent of Fairfax and he's got to face up to running it because I don't think there's any buyer there, certainly at a premium," Murdoch said.
"He's a very successful publisher in other countries and there's no reason why he shouldn't be very successful with Fairfax," the Courier-Mail quoted Murdoch as saying.
"But he's frustrated because he's only got 25 percent which doesn't give clear control of the board," he said.
"Mr Packer has two or three people there on the board who are sort of trying to thwart him or push their weight around in things like editorial policy," Murdoch said.
"But we're not interested. We're very happy with what we've got," Murdoch said.
